title: stability-annotations-ops-brief-2029-07-02
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a compact week-in-review for the SRE group covering incidents, SLO health, on-call handoffs, and outstanding operational actions. Intended to be consumed by SRE, infra, and platform-eng leads before the 7/3 stability sync.

TL;DR:
- Two customer-impact incidents this week (partial degradation to hosted generation and delayed KV cache warmups).
- Platform P95 generation latency breached SLO on two short windows; error budget usage ~7% for the rolling 28d window.
- On-call handoffs were noisy during the Tue 03:30 UTC window; improvements to routing rules and alert thresholds are proposed.
- Immediate action: cap concurrent long-running backfills and enable incremental KV cache population for Dedicated pools.

Incidents (chronological):
1) INC-2029-345 — "generation-throttle-spike" (2029-06-30 03:25 UTC)
   - User impact: ~12% of calls returned 429/timeout for ~18 minutes across hosted-api region-us-west1. Intermittent client retries amplified load.
   - Detection: alert p95_generation_latency > 800ms and request success rate dip triggered pager.
   - Root cause (initial): upstream autoscaler reacted to ephemeral CPU spikes on a subset of model workers causing temporary unavailability; autoscaler configuration allowed scale-downs during short load bursts.
   - Mitigation performed: temporarily raised min-replicas for affected pool and enabled elastic-burst buffer for 45 minutes.
   - Follow-ups: (a) tighten HPA cooldown to 2m (owner: Marcus Patel), (b) implement request-level rate limiter to reduce retry storms (owner: Rina Gomez), (c) postmortem draft due 2029-07-06.

2) INC-2029-351 — "kv-warmup-lag" (2029-07-01 12:10 UTC)
   - User impact: Minor — single-customer tail latency (p99) observed on consecutive long-chat sessions; manifests as 200–600ms added latency.
   - Detection: internal customer-reported ticket + kv-cache hit-rate drop correlated with spike in cold sequence lengths.
   - Root cause: large dedicated-pool job evicted popular KV shards during a one-off model rollout. KV population paths didn't rehydrate fast enough; background population job had low concurrency.
   - Mitigation: re-prioritized KV rehydration and rolled back rollout for the affected model variant.
   - Follow-ups: (a) add proactive KV-populate step in rollout pipeline (owner: Owen Park), (b) add metrics and an alert for KV fill-rate < 70% for 10m (owner: Alyssa Chen).

SLO snapshot and short analysis:
- Generation API (hosted)
  - Objective: 99th percentile latency < 750ms (rolling 28d)
  - Current: 98.6% compliance (error budget used ~7%)
  - Notes: Recent traffic pattern changes (batch uploader coupled with aggressive client retries) increased request burstiness.
- Embeddings API
  - Objective: success rate >= 99.95%
  - Current: 99.98% (fine)
- KV cache availability
  - Objective: availability >= 99.9%
  - Current: 99.7% last 7d (dip due to kv-warmup-lag)

Operational observations and suggestions:
- Alert fatigue: The Tue morning cascade shows our current alert thresholds for scale/CPU are too sensitive to short-lived spikes. Recommend evaluation of "burst windows" — i.e., require threshold to hold for 90s before paging. (Proposer: Marcus)
- Retry storms: client SDK retries are exponential but with low jitter; recommend adding token-bucket enforcement at ingress and a soft 2s client-side backoff template in SDK docs. (Owner: Rina)
- Rollout safety: integrate a KV warmup job into model rollout recipe and gate rollout progress on KV rehydrate % for the top 95% prefixes. (Owner: Owen)
- Playbook gaps: the current runbook for "generation latency spike" lacks a quick checklist for validating autoscaler cooldowns and in-flight queue depth; we should add a short diagnostic that on-call can run in <3 minutes. (Owner: Alyssa)

On-call handoff notes (this rotation):
- Outgoing (2029-06-30 08:00 UTC) — left note: observed repeated autoscaler alerts; tuned min-replicas up; flagged JIRA-OPS-932 for autoscaler tuning.
- Incoming (2029-07-02 08:00 UTC) — incoming should review slow-start jobs (backfills) and ensure none overlap with peak client upload windows.
- Pager etiquette: when an alert triggers, include the latest autoscaler dashboard link and the relevant model-pool id in the first message to speed triage.

Action items (short-term, owners, ETA):
- HPA cooldown change to 2m (Marcus Patel) — ETA 2029-07-04
- Rate-limiter prototype at ingress for retry storms (Rina Gomez) — prototype ETA 2029-07-09
- KV populate step in rollout (Owen Park) — design doc ETA 2029-07-08
- Add KV fill-rate alert and dashboard tile (Alyssa Chen) — ETA 2029-07-05
- Create 3-min diagnostic checklist for generation-latency runbook (Alyssa Chen) — ETA 2029-07-04

Longer-term notes (for roadmap sync):
- Capacity planning: Dedicated pools need a small reserved headroom (% spare tokens) for model rollouts to avoid eviction cascades. Propose a small reserved capacity feature in Dedicated offering — ops and product sync needed.
- Observability: invest in better per-customer heatmaps (sequence length vs latency) to detect heavy-tail workloads before SLO hit.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we relax autoscaler sensitivity globally or target specific pools? (Ops preference: target first.)
- Small chance that adding ingress rate-limits affects legit high-throughput customers; need staged rollout and feature flag.

Meeting cadence and next steps:
- Review postmortem for INC-2029-345 on 2029-07-06 (30m) — invite: SRE, infra, platform-eng, product-hosted-api.
- Follow-up stability sync on 2029-07-10 to review action item progress and SLO trend post-changes.

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to include the model-pool id in any slack alerts; it saves 5–10 mins in triage.
- Draft wording for the SDK backoff suggestion — keep it short and prescriptive.

Appendix (quick links and dashboards):
- Autoscaler dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/autoscaler
- KV metrics: https://grafana.internal/d/kv-populate
- Recent traces sample (generation spike): https://jaeger.internal/trace/abcdef123456

End of brief.
